LiAlO2 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium aluminate. Al3+ is in its highest oxidation state and is very hard to reduce, so it should resist the Li6PS5Cl sulfide. Its Li-O-Al framework is oxidatively robust, which should limit decomposition and space-charge formation at LiCoO2 under 4.0 V, giving a low chemical penalty. It is a different cation family from the earlier phosphate, niobate and silicate ideas.
